{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-fcv6","title":"[rereview] project-LICHEN-a4n2.3: nonce consumed before tx_queue_push — seqnum leak on ENOBUFS","description":"In lichen_link_tx() (lichen_link_tx.c:124-178), the nonce (epoch, seqnum) is allocated by lichen_link_next_tx() at line 124, BEFORE the tx_queue_push_default_deadline() call at line 174. If tx_queue_push fails (e.g., queue full with same-priority frames, returning -ENOBUFS), the function returns the error but the nonce has already been consumed. There is no lichen_link_release_tx() rollback mechanism. The caller will retry, consuming another nonce, causing a sequence-number gap.

This is not a security vulnerability (receivers handle seq gaps), but it is a correctness issue: a nonce is permanently lost per ENOBUFS failure, and in the worst case with sustained backpressure, the node could exhaust its nonce space faster than intended.

Fix options:
1. Add a lichen_link_release_tx() that decrements seqnum / rewinds epoch on failure
2. Restructure lichen_link_tx() to push first, then allocate nonce only on success
3. Pass the already-built frame directly to the radio on ENOBUFS instead of returning error (bypass the queue)","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"agent@lichen-project.dev","created_at":"2026-07-24T14:18:47.517133617Z","created_by":"AI Agent","updated_at":"2026-07-24T14:18:47.517133617Z"}
